title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall

vibeProfile.oneLine: A widow's secret: she fled a cruel husband to save herself and her son.

summary: A mysterious young widow arrives at Wildfell Hall with her small son and sets the local gossips talking, until her diary reveals the truth: she has fled a dissolute, abusive husband to protect herself and her child. Anne Bronte's second novel was startlingly frank for its time about alcoholism, marital cruelty and a woman's right to leave, and was long overshadowed by her sisters' work. Bold and morally serious, it is now recognised as an early feminist landmark.
whyReadIt: The boldest Bronte, a frank Victorian novel about leaving an abusive marriage. An early feminist landmark, long underrated.

funFacts.text: It was so frank about marital abuse that Anne's own sister Charlotte suppressed its reprinting.
